hard_fail_reasons: Bench and tool-board visibility scores 1/5 at the 64-inch Room A gameplay camera.

incumbent_comparison: First Scavenger Work Area candidate against the current generic presentation. The salvaged materials and supported frame establish a Scavenger shelter, but the 64-inch Room A view reads primarily as a roofed shelter and does not show the hand-work function.
next_action_hypothesis: Shorten the camera-facing roof depth and overhang by about one third, raise the front eave within the 9-inch envelope, and place the blue tool board and large hand tools in a clearly visible band above the bench. Keep the front entrance open and preserve visible roof supports.

observations.close_up_quality: The close render shows supported framing and a constructed roof, but the broad canopy continues to hide most work-bench details.

observations.proportion: The full-width, full-depth roof carries too much visual weight relative to the bench and tool board.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot validates 22.81 x 8.045 x 11.48 inches against the 23 x 9 x 12 inch envelope, but the roof-to-work-surface proportion does not preserve the target's gameplay read.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The structure is identifiable as a salvage shelter but the bench/tool board are hidden, so the work-area function does not read at gameplay scale.
observations.silhouette_quality: The broad sheet canopy dominates the 64-inch front and side views; the structure resembles a generic open shelter and overlaps visually with the Depot.
observations.surface_variation: The roof patches and timber show some material variation, but the work-function pieces remain visually obscured.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 imports and renders the candidate through the review-only resolver in actual Room A. Validation reports one mesh object, seven material surfaces, 15,444 triangles, and bounds within the envelope.
